accepted.evidence: Turner7031 section1 explicitly gives Poguli nāht beside Kishtawari nasth. The table naht has the same diagnostic consonant order; its unmarked vowel length is preserved. Do not assign this ht form to the separate nakka family. Source image and reviewed import row checked; no source transcription or identity changes.

Turner6909 gives neighbouring Rambani/Ḍoḍi and Bhalessi nakk, Kashmiri nākh and wider nak forms. Siraji nak matches this k-family; Turner leaves its deeper derivation from nas-ka or nast-ka uncertain. Source image and reviewed import row checked; no source transcription or identity changes.

Turner10180 section1 gives Lahnda/Punjabi mucch and nearby much/mūch moustache, supporting Siraji mucʰ rather than the o-vowel section2. Turner explicitly leaves the formation open between gōcchā influenced by mukha and MIA massu from śmaśru. Source image and reviewed import row checked; no source transcription or identity changes.

Turner4269 gives Prakrit guṁchā moustache, Kashmiri gõch and Savi gōčē. Poguli gucʰe fits this regional g-initial moustache family; its unmarked nasalisation and u vowel are retained. The proposed connection with guccha cluster is uncertain, so no direct link to that broader bunch-word entry is substituted. Source image and reviewed import row checked; no source transcription or identity changes.
